name: French Open
stakes: This week, PV Sindhu's pursuit of a Super 750 title in Paris could provide a significant boost for Indian badminton, while others look to build momentum for future tournaments.
summary:
India's campaign at the French Open has been a mixed bag, highlighted by a stellar run from **PV Sindhu**. The former world champion has battled her way into the Women's Singles final, showcasing her resilience with a hard-fought semifinal victory over Japan's Hina Akechi. She now faces the formidable An Se-young in what promises to be a thrilling championship decider. This deep run marks a significant moment for Sindhu, who is aiming for her first Super 750 title in quite some time.

On the Men's Doubles front, top Indian pair **Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty** faced an unexpected early exit, falling in the Round of 32. This was a disappointing start for the highly-ranked duo, who would have hoped for a much longer stay in the tournament. Young talent Unnati Hooda also bowed out in the opening round of Women's Singles, while the promising Women's Doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand's draw details remain TBD, indicating their journey might have concluded earlier or their match details are not yet available. Overall, it's Sindhu carrying the flag high for India in Paris.
